NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The proposed intervention is to replace one standard activated-alumina cartridge in the side-loop filtration system with a chelating resin cartridge to preferentially bind copper ions while maintaining oxidation control. Standard practice uses activated-alumina cartridges solely for oxidation byproduct removal; this intervention introduces a second capture mechanism that selectively targets dissolved copper ions without requiring additional hardware, a departure from single-function filtration. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is using mixed-bed resins in power plant condensate systems, but those are designed for broad ion removal and require complete system redesign, whereas this intervention uses a targeted chelation mechanism in existing cartridge form factors. The mechanism exploits the preferential affinity of iminodiacetate functional groups for copper ions (Cu²⁺ > H⁺), reducing dissolved copper concentration while the alumina continues to handle acidic oxidation byproducts.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation is the Nernst distribution law for chelation: K_d = [Cu²⁺]_resin / [Cu²⁺]_fluid, where iminodiacetate resins exhibit K_d > 10⁴ for copper at 55°C. For a 38-server system with 1.2 m³ fluid volume and 50 ppm copper contamination, a 10" chelating resin cartridge (≈2.5 L resin, capacity ≈1.2 eq/L) can reduce [Cu²⁺] by >90% (from 50 ppm to <5 ppm) before saturation, directly addressing the copper dissolution failure mechanism while maintaining the existing alumina's oxidation control function.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- Replace one existing activated-alumina cartridge with a standard iminodiacetate chelating resin cartridge (b) [net hardware: 0; uses existing cartridge housing]
- Adjust side-loop flow rate to 15% of total loop flow (c) [parameter change; no new hardware]
- Extend cartridge replacement interval to 6 months (c) [procedure change; leverages existing maintenance schedule]

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Standard practice: 2 activated-alumina cartridges replaced quarterly (8/year) + 6 hours downtime/year
Proposed intervention: 1 alumina + 1 chelating resin cartridge replaced biannually (4 cartridges/year) + 6 hours downtime/year
Burden class: Same (identical downtime, fewer cartridge changes, no new hardware, no new skills required)

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Install test loop with identical copper coupon and fluid sample; monitor copper concentration via ICP-MS and fluid colorimetry weekly for 90 days.
Instruments: ICP-MS for copper quantification, spectrophotometer for colorimetry, flowmeter.
Pass/fail: Copper reduction >80% vs control (untreated fluid) and fluid color improvement (ΔE < 2.0) within 30 days.
Duration: 90 days (covers 2 cartridge service intervals).
Kill criterion: If copper reduction <50% or fluid darkening continues at >80% of original rate after 30 days, falsify the intervention.

BILL_UNTAGGED: - Replaces one activated-alumina cartridge with chelating resin (no net hardware addition)
- Uses existing infrastructure (side-loop, housing, downtime budget)
- Adds only a procedural flow adjustment during service
1. Install chelating resin cartridge in parallel with existing activated-alumina cartridge
- Acid number (ASTM D974, pass threshold: rise <0.02 mgKOH/g/month)
- Dielectric strength (ASTM D877, pass threshold: >50 kV)
3. Compare to baseline (no resin) for 6 months.
